findings.text: the two new tests exercise only the closed-form re-read, so a regression restoring a hardcoded authored zero or dropping the terminal reader wiring in benchmarks/oracle_start_newton_probe.py:2087-2090 would pass the suite while the fixed-point clause went back to a confounded comparison.

a missing or non-finite compensating_field_t is coerced to zeros unconditionally, so a corrupt positive receipt re-reads as a zero actuator contribution rather than refusing; the constrained flag is already read from the same stored record and the fallback could be limited to the unconstrained arm.

the analytic_authored_axis_flux_wb and analytic_authored_boundary_flux_wb keys fall back via .get to the read's own axis and boundary levels, so the key name asserts a basis the value may not carry; on the only live call path the state is analytic so the figures are correct, but the substitution is unmarked for a later reader.

the split "the compensator's own field accounts for 0.1597 Wb of it; the remaining 0.6670 Wb is the equilibrium the row reached" is first-order: the receipt subtracts the closed-form column at the two points, and nothing separates the plasma's own response to the applied 2.4 mT field, so the residual also carries that response and is an upper estimate rather than a measured separation.
